chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Abdillah ibn al-Mughirah, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who slept through the 'Isha prayer and did not rise until after the middle of the night, he said: 'He prays it and becomes a fasting person in the morning.'

key_terms.يُصَلِّيهَا: He prays it (referring to the makeup prayer)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who misses Isha prayer due to sleep and wakes up late?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes fasting as the expiation (Kaffarah) for missing the 'Isha prayer due to sleep until after midnight. This ruling highlights the severity of neglecting the evening prayer, linking the missed obligation directly to the spiritual discipline of fasting, a practice deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence for compensating for specific lapses in worship.
